topic: Are sentiment classifiers sensitive to negation words on short movie reviews (SST-2)?

review.Summary: The paper investigates whether sentiment classifiers are sensitive to negation words in short movie reviews from the SST-2 dataset. It uses Llama-3 to evaluate performance on original and modified datasets. However, the results section is incomplete, and the experimental design lacks statistical rigor.
Strengths: Use of a relevant benchmark dataset (SST-2)
Exploration of both negation addition and removal conditions
Weaknesses: Incomplete results section: no performance metrics for modified datasets
No statistical analysis (e.g., t-tests) to assess significance
Small dataset size (500 samples) may limit generalizability
Lack of robustness in the experimental setup (e.g., no hyperparameter tuning)
Computational constraints may affect the validity of findings
Questions: Why were the results for the modified datasets not fully computed?
What statistical methods were used to assess the significance of the results?
How does the small dataset size affect the generalizability of the findings?
Limitations: Small dataset size (500 samples) may not represent the full SST-2 dataset
Computational constraints limited the execution of the experiments
Lack of statistical analysis to support conclusions

trace.interpretation:
The results indicate that the model's performance on the original SST-2 dataset has an accuracy of 0.85 and an F1 score of 0.83. However, the metrics for the modified datasets (negation addition and removal) are not provided. To interpret the results accurately, we need to compare the accuracy and F1 scores for the original dataset with those for the modified datasets. For instance, if the accuracy drops significantly when negation words are added, it suggests that the model is sensitive to these words. Conversely, if the accuracy improves when negation words are removed, it indicates that the model is more sensitive to their absence. We should also conduct statistical tests, such as t-tests, to determine the significance of any observed differences in performance. Additionally, we should ensure that the results are properly formatted and include all relevant metrics to support the interpretation.
